parties: Waaree Renewable Technologies Limited acquires 55% stake in Associated Power Structures Private Limited from Desai Family Trust, Kothari Family Trust, Patel Family Trust, and select promoter individuals
headline: Waaree Renewable acquires 55% controlling stake in power infrastructure firm APSPL for ₹1,225 crore via mixed primary-secondary transaction
sum: Waaree Renewable Technologies completed a ₹1,225 crore acquisition of 55% stake in Associated Power Structures, making APSPL a subsidiary. The deal, executed through combined issuance of fresh shares and purchase of existing shares from promoter family trusts, strengthens Waaree's integrated renewable energy and power transmission infrastructure platform as part of its 'Waaree 2.0' strategy.
implication: Mixed primary-secondary equity acquisition with registered valuer pricing on fresh issuance exemplifies structuring discipline for unquoted acquisitions; family trust sellers and locked-in shareholder agreements signal clear promoter monetisation within family-controlled business models.
detail: WRTL acquired both newly issued equity shares and existing shares held by the Desai, Kothari, and Patel family trusts, plus founder Ajay Patel, in a two-tier structure: Share Purchase and Subscription Agreement (covering fresh issuance and secondary purchase) and Shareholders Agreement (governing inter-se director nomination, pre-emptive rights, and capital structure restrictions post-acquisition). APSPL, founded 1996, operates in power transmission tower fabrication, galvanised structures, and EPC services with ₹1,226 crore FY25 revenue and ₹339 crore net worth. The acquisition realigns Waaree's strategy from pure solar EPC toward integrated end-to-end renewable generation, transmission, and evacuation—deemed critical as India's renewable capacity scales and transmission bottlenecks emerge.

structure.novel: Dual-track primary-secondary transaction structure combining fresh share issuance at FMV valuer price with cash/equity buyout of family trust holdings in single closing; Shareholders Agreement post-acquisition allocates board seats and pre-emptive rights, creating formal governance framework for minority co-shareholders (remaining 45%) alongside new subsidiary status.
